To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the mother‐cell and forespore protein networks are responsible for the localization of SpoIVF, a key protein for the activation of σF in the forespores, in the septal membranes of the sporangia.

the mother‐cell sporulation protein SpoIVFA is anchored in the sporulation septal membrane by a web of protein–protein interactions that include proteins made in the forespores as well as proteins made in the mother cell.
SpoIVFA localizes to the septum through a network of protein–protein interactions that are established along and across the sporulation membrane.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding how proteins localize to the septum during sporulation in B. subtilis.
the mechanisms of protein localization in the sporulation septa of B. subtilis and how these mechanisms are integrated with other processes of sporulation.
understanding how proteins are anchored at specific sites within a cell.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the mechanism by which SpoIVFA is anchored at the mother cell side of the septum is through a network of proteins that interact across the septum.
SpoIVFA localization in the septum is achieved through a complex network of protein interactions across the septum and along the membrane.
the subcellular localization of SpoIVF is achieved through a web of interactions along and/or across the septum.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a web of interactions is involved in protein localization and anchoring at the septum and this web of interactions is held in place by a zipper‐like mechanism across the septum.
the subcellular localization of proteins in B. subtilis is achieved by a network of interactions among proteins in the mother cell and foresporge compartments.
the localization of a membrane protein is achieved by the sum of its protein–protein interactions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the localization of a sporangium protein is achieved through the coordinated action of a network of interacting proteins.
the subcellular localization of proteins is achieved through a web of interactions among the proteins involved.
a web of protein–protein interactions is a common mechanism for the localization of membrane proteins to the septum.
